fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: October inflation of 3.8% and an upgrade to US GDP figures keep a December rise on the table, and the minutes showed almost all officials expect more hikes. The open question is size: Goolsbee has left a larger-than-usual rise open, while CME FedWatch shows zero chance of a half-point move.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: This year's summit sits under a US presidency and follows a crowded month: Trump met Xi and Putin at a summit in Shenzhen billed around nuclear arms, while COP31 ran into overtime over a fossil fuel deadlock. The leaders' meeting is the first time that wider table sits down together since.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: Euro countries picked Pablo Hernández de Cos over Klaas Knot to succeed Christine Lagarde, and Germany took the chief economist seat for Markus Brunnermeier, so the council decides with its next leadership already named. France's borrowing premium over Germany sits at 1.75 points, and the ECB has so far left it to markets.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: UK inflation accelerated again and has now run above the Bank of England's target for more than two years, so the committee meets with prices moving away from its goal rather than toward it. This meeting settles how long it is prepared to tolerate that overshoot before UK borrowers carry the cost.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: Tokyo core prices rose 2.9%, the fastest since July 2025, days after the national reading undershot forecast at 2.2%. Meanwhile the yen breached 160, Washington sold $500 million of euros to buy it, and the weak currency is swelling the bill for Japan's defence plan and its flagship AI project. The board must decide which signal to answer.

fred-us-gdp-2026-12-02.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's measure of US output, published each quarter as an advance estimate and then revised twice. It sets the growth figure the Federal Reserve, Treasury yields and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-gdp-2026-12-02.recent: A 4.3% growth revision drew Trump's charge that his own Commerce Department published 'fake' figures before the midterms, and a demand for an investigation. The same upgrade kept a December rate rise in play for the Fed, so this release is read twice: for the Fed's path, and for whether the agency's numbers still carry weight.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-12-04.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly Employment Situation report, usually out on the first Friday, counts nonfarm payrolls and sets the unemployment rate. Treasury yields, the dollar and Fed rate bets move on it within seconds.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-12-04.recent: This release carries the latest monthly payroll count and unemployment rate, and revises the two months before it. It settles whether US hiring held its pace through the month.
